name: scrollable-region
description: A region that scrolls because its content overflows the box it is given, and that a keyboard must therefore be able to reach and move. APG has no pattern page for it, confirmed against the pattern index rather than assumed, because scrolling is a behaviour of a box and not a widget; WCAG 2.1.1 is the pattern's source instead, on the plainest reading of it there is. Content that only a pointer can bring into view is content a keyboard user cannot reach at all, and a row of cards that runs past its right edge is exactly that. The group role and its name are the other half: a tab stop that announces nothing is a landing a reader cannot account for.

requires.roles.element: group -- the region is one thing containing several, and group is what says so without claiming a structure a reader can walk
requires.roles.label: an aria-label or aria-labelledby naming what the region holds, since a group announced as a group alone tells a reader that focus moved and nothing about where
requires.focus.stop: the container is itself in the tab order, so the arrow keys scroll it once focus lands. A scrollable box that is not focusable is the failure this pattern exists to name, and it is invisible to everyone who tests with a pointer
